source: Energy is what makes things move, light up, heat up or make sound. Its forms include motion, stored (in food, batteries, a stretched rubber band or something high up), heat, light, sound and electrical energy.
Thinking only moving things have energy. A book on a high shelf, a battery and a sandwich all have stored energy.
A running dog, a glowing lamp, a ringing bell and a warm stove all have something in common: energy.
Energy is what makes things move, light up, heat up or make sound. It comes in many forms.
The faster something moves, the more motion energy it has. A fast ball hits harder than a slow one.
A child holds a stretched slingshot band, then lets go and the pebble flies. What forms of energy are there?
Stored energy, then motion (and a little sound).
The stretched band holds stored energy.
When it snaps back, the pebble gets motion energy.
The snap makes a little sound.
Thinking only moving things have energy. Food has stored energy that your body uses, and a ball held high has stored energy that turns into motion when it falls.
